label: History
value: Anne Shirley arrives at Green Gables in Avonlea, Prince Edward Island.
unit: Anne Shirley arrives at Green Gables in Avonlea, Prince Edward Island, due to a mix-up by the orphan asylum, as Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert intended to adopt a boy to help on the farm. Though Marilla initially plans to send her back, Matthew's quiet affection and Anne's spirited charm persuade Marilla to keep her. Anne quickly makes a bosom friend in Diana Barry, attends school, and ignites a long-standing feud with Gilbert Blythe after he calls her 'Carrots.' Through various scrapes and mishaps, Anne proves her worth, excels academically, wins the Avery Scholarship at Queen's Academy, and loses her dear guardian Matthew to a fatal heart attack. Deciding to forgo college to stay at Green Gables and care for Marilla's failing eyesight, Anne takes the teaching position at Avonlea School after Gilbert generously surrenders it for her. As Avonlea's schoolteacher, Anne helps establish the Village Improvement Society, adopts the orphaned twins Davy and Dora Keith with Marilla, and successfully manages her classroom. By the end of her second year teaching, Anne forgives Gilbert, cementing a warm friendship with him while continuing to cherish her life at Green Gables.

value: Anthony Pye attends Avonlea School
unit: Anthony Pye attends Avonlea School during the time Anne Shirley becomes its teacher. Encouraged by his family's belief that women cannot discipline schoolboys effectively, Anthony behaves defiantly and tests Anne's patience continuously during her first year. His persistent disobedience culminates in an incident where Anne loses her temper and whips him, an act she immediately regrets. Unexpectedly, this firm punishment wins Anthony's respect, causing him to become one of Anne's most obedient and devoted pupils for the rest of her tenure as teacher.

label: History
value: Charlotta the Fourth was hired to live with Miss Lavender Lewis.
unit: Charlotta the Fourth was hired to live with and assist Miss Lavender Lewis at Echo Lodge in Grafton. When Anne Shirley and Diana Barry accidentally discover Echo Lodge, Charlotta welcomes them and manages the hospitality alongside Miss Lavender. She quickly forms an affection for Anne and helps facilitate visits between the Avonlea schoolteacher and her mistress. During the romance and subsequent wedding of Miss Lavender and Stephen Irving, Charlotta is overjoyed by her mistress's happiness. Following the wedding, she goes to live with the newly married couple in Boston to continue serving them.

label: History
value: Diana Barry becomes Anne Shirley's primary companion.
unit: Diana Barry becomes Anne Shirley's primary companion shortly after Anne arrives in Avonlea, swearing an oath of eternal friendship. Their early friendship faces a trial when Diana accidentally gets drunk on Marilla's raspberry cordial during a tea party, leading Mrs. Barry to temporarily forbid them from speaking. Diana is restored to her mother's favor after Anne saves Diana's younger sister Minnie May from croup. Diana attends the Avonlea school alongside Anne and joins her in various childhood adventures, including the Story Club. When Anne leaves for Queen's Academy to pursue her teaching certificate, Diana remains at home as her parents do not send her to advanced studies, though the two maintain a close bond. During Anne's time teaching in Avonlea, Diana remains her primary confidante and joins the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, while also beginning a courtship with Fred Wright.

Their early friendship faces a trial when Diana accidentally gets drunk on Marilla's raspberry cordial during a tea party, leading Mrs. Barry to temporarily forbid them from speaking. Diana is restored to her mother's favor after Anne saves Diana's younger sister Minnie May from croup. Diana attends the Avonlea school alongside Anne and joins her in various childhood adventures, including the Story Club. When Anne leaves for Queen's Academy to pursue her teaching certificate, Diana remains at home as her parents do not send her to advanced studies, though the two maintain a close bond. During Anne's time teaching in Avonlea, Diana remains her primary confidante and joins the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, while also beginning a courtship with Fred Wright.

label: History
value: Following the death of Mary Keith, Dora is taken in by Marilla Cuthbert at Green Gables.
unit: Following the death of her mother, Mary Keith, Dora and her twin brother Davy are taken in by Marilla Cuthbert at Green Gables. Marilla initially plans to keep them only until Mary's brother, Uncle Richard, arrives to claim them, but he dies in western Canada. Dora's flawless behavior makes her very easy to care for, though Anne Shirley and Marilla find her somewhat uninteresting compared to her mischievous brother. Dora attends Avonlea School and steadily performs her duties without complaint or incident. She remains living at Green Gables as a well-mannered, quiet child.

label: History
value: Gilbert returns to Avonlea School
unit: Gilbert returns to Avonlea School after a period away and immediately notices new student Anne Shirley. When he teases her by calling her 'Carrots' and pulling her red hair, Anne smashes a slate over his head, starting a years-long rivalry as Gilbert tries repeatedly to apologize and earn her forgiveness. Throughout their school years and Queen's Academy studies, Gilbert and Anne compete for top academic honors, though Gilbert's admiration for her only grows. Upon graduating from Queen's with a teacher's license, Gilbert gives up his secured position at the Avonlea school to Anne so she can live at Green Gables after Matthew Cuthbert's death, taking the White Sands school instead. Touched by his sacrifice, Anne finally forgives him, and the two become close friends. Over the next two years while teaching, Gilbert helps form the Avonlea Village Improvement Society alongside Anne and eventually decides to attend Redmond College to pursue a medical degree.

label: History
value: Mr. James Harrison moves into the farm next to Green Gables.
unit: Mr. James Harrison moves into the farm next to Green Gables at the beginning of Anne Shirley's tenure as the Avonlea schoolteacher. His initial meeting with Anne is contentious when she confronts him after her jersey cow breaks into his oat field, leading to a sharp exchange of insults. However, the two quickly reconcile and become warm friends, spending many pleasant afternoons chatting on his veranda. Anne discovers that he owns a foul-mouthed parrot named Ginger, who constantly insults visitors until its eventual death. Later, Mr. Harrison's estranged wife, Emily Isabella, arrives unexpectedly in Avonlea, revealing that he had left New Brunswick following a marital misunderstanding rather than being a lifelong bachelor. With Anne's gentle encouragement and assistance, Mr. Harrison reconciles with his wife, who cleans up his house and settles down with him in Avonlea.

value: Josie Pye attends Avonlea School.

Later, Josie joins the Queen's Academy preparation class taught by Miss Stacy and successfully passes the entrance exams to earn her teacher's license. After completing her studies at Queen's, she secures a position teaching at a local school in the Avonlea area.

label: History
value: Miss Lavendar was engaged to Stephen Irving.
unit: In her youth, Miss Lavendar was engaged to Stephen Irving, but a hasty quarrel caused by her pride led to their breakup, after which Stephen left the area and eventually married someone else. For twenty-five years, she lived a quiet, secluded life at Echo Lodge in Grafton, sustained by her rich imagination and fictional companions. Anne Shirley and Diana Barry discover her home by chance while walking in Grafton and quickly bond with her over their shared love of romance and imagination. Anne later introduces Stephen Irving's son, Paul Irving, to Miss Lavendar, and the two form a fond attachment. Realizing that Stephen Irving is now a widower, Anne facilitates a reunion between Stephen and Miss Lavendar when Stephen returns to Prince Edward Island. The former lovers reconcile their past misunderstandings, renew their romance, and are married at Echo Lodge before departing for Boston.

label: History
value: Marilla lives at Green Gables
unit: Marilla lives at Green Gables with her unmarried brother, Matthew. Deciding they need help on the farm as they age, they arrange to adopt an orphan boy from Nova Scotia, but receive an imaginative young girl named Anne Shirley by mistake. Though Marilla initially intends to send Anne back, she relents and agrees to raise her, taking on the responsibility of her upbringing with strict discipline. Over the next several years, Marilla comes to love Anne deeply, though she conceals the extent of her affection. When Matthew dies suddenly of a heart attack following a bank failure, Marilla faces severe strain and failing eyesight, threatening her ability to keep Green Gables. Anne gives up her college scholarship to stay in Avonlea and teach, allowing Marilla to keep her home. Later, Marilla takes in the orphaned twins of her distant relative Mary Keith—Davy and Dora—and raises them with Anne's assistance.

label: History
value: Matthew and Marilla decide to adopt an orphan boy.
unit: Matthew and his sister Marilla decide to adopt an orphan boy to help Matthew with the farm work as his health begins to fail. When Matthew travels to the Bright River station, he finds that an eleven-year-old girl, Anne Shirley, was sent by mistake. Enchanted by her bright chatter and spirit during the ride home, Matthew immediately wants to keep her. He quietly persuades Marilla to let Anne stay at Green Gables, becoming her constant champion and confidant. Over the next few years, Matthew indulges Anne, famously buying her a dress with puff sleeves when he notices she feels different from other girls. When Anne earns a scholarship to Queen's Academy and excels in her studies, Matthew takes immense pride in her accomplishments. Shortly after Anne completes her studies at Queen's and returns home, Matthew suffers a sudden, fatal heart attack upon reading that the Abbey Bank, where his savings were kept, has failed. His death deeply mourned by Anne, Marilla, and the entire Avonlea community.

label: History
value: Paul Irving arrives in Avonlea
unit: Paul Irving arrives in Avonlea to live with his paternal grandmother, Mrs. Irving, after spending his earlier childhood in Boston following his mother's death. When Anne Shirley takes her position as the Avonlea schoolteacher, she instantly recognizes Paul as a kindred spirit due to his vivid imagination and love of beauty. Paul forms a strong bond with Anne, sharing his secret imaginary friends—such as the Rock People and his double, 'Good Paul'—and confiding his deepest feelings to her. During his time in Avonlea, he longs for his father, Stephen Irving, who works away in the United States. Anne later facilitates the reunion of Stephen Irving and his old love, Lavender Lewis; as a result, Stephen marries Miss Lavender, giving Paul a beloved new mother and a happy family life.

label: History
value: Mr. Phillips serves as the schoolteacher in Avonlea
unit: Mr. Phillips serves as the schoolteacher in Avonlea during Anne Shirley's early years at Green Gables. On Anne's first day of school, he misspells her name as 'Ann' on the blackboard and punishes her for being late by forcing her to sit with Gilbert Blythe, triggering Anne's long-standing grudge against Gilbert. He routinely neglects his general duties to spend time courting one of his older pupils, Prissie Andrews. Later, he forms an advanced class to prepare older students, including Anne and Gilbert, for the Queen's Academy entrance examinations. At the end of the school term, he leaves Avonlea, giving a tearful farewell speech that leaves his pupils surprisingly moved despite his poor treatment of them.

After graduating, Ruby takes a teaching position at Carmody School. During her time as a teacher, she continues her keen interest in courtship, boasting to her friends about her numerous beaux and romantic conquests.

label: History
value: Miss Muriel Stacy arrives in Avonlea
unit: Miss Muriel Stacy arrives in Avonlea to take over the local school after the departure of Mr. Phillips. Her novel teaching methods, which include nature study on Friday afternoons and physical exercises, initially cause a stir among the conservative members of the village, but she quickly wins over the community through her pupils' evident progress and enthusiasm. Recognizing potential in her advanced pupils, she organizes a special 'Queen's Class' to prepare students like Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe for the entrance examination to Queen's Academy. Throughout the school year, she provides unwavering encouragement and extra tuition to her students. Her mentorship enables Anne and her classmates to pass their examinations with high honors. After her successful tenure in Avonlea, Miss Stacy accepts a teaching position at a higher-grade school in Charlottetown, leaving behind a lasting impression on Anne, who continues to view her as a role model.

Her novel teaching methods, which include nature study on Friday afternoons and physical exercises, initially cause a stir among the conservative members of the village, but she quickly wins over the community through her pupils' evident progress and enthusiasm. Recognizing potential in her advanced pupils, she organizes a special 'Queen's Class' to prepare students like Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe for the entrance examination to Queen's Academy. Throughout the school year, she provides unwavering encouragement and extra tuition to her students. Her mentorship enables Anne and her classmates to pass their examinations with high honors. After her successful tenure in Avonlea, Miss Stacy accepts a teaching position at a higher-grade school in Charlottetown, leaving behind a lasting impression on Anne, who continues to view her as a role model.
